COHERENT GROUP FILTER
For commuting involutions R=-Z_p Z_q and S=SWAP_pq Z_a, coherent fresh check ancillas and controlled conjugations give per full-memory Kraus K the accepted average E_S E_R(K)=(K+RKR+SKS+RSKRS)/4. It commutes with both R and S. On Q, SWAP=I so S=Z_a and no0-to1 detector block survives; on P, SWAP=X_L so the accepted detector block has the Y/Z structure. The earlier U1041 complete-memory checker supplies this abstract primitive if its own controlled-involution, fresh-flag and noise conditions are actually satisfied for both checks. Classical randomization averages CP maps and cannot replace a coherent Kraus average.
A complete-boundary joint Stinespring deviation<=xi, with normalized Bell embedding and zero ideal forbidden components, bounds their unnormalized total effect by xi^2 I via orthogonal projection/Bessel. Per-branch tolerances, isolated endpoint errors, conditional-on-rare-success errors and availability are separate. The source8/10-gate netlists and simulations are unacquired and not independently accepted here.
An exact failure witness is Q input with R=-I, S=Z_a and U=X_a. The ideal group filter vanishes there; classical conjugation randomization still flips the detector with certainty. If the bath dephases both check ancillas between their controlled gates, the accepted++ probability is1/4 and every accepted detector is a false click. This is an exact small dilation/counterexample, not a replay of the missing producer study.

## ASTRA — Coherently enforcing quantum symmetry

The strongest new construction replaces an assumed Hamiltonian symmetry with an active, heralded symmetry filter.

The previous service required the complete detector interaction to conserve the protected rail sector and commute with the combined rail–ancilla symmetry. The new construction can enforce those conditions on the accepted quantum operation, even when the underlying interaction violates them.

Let \\(U\\) be the complete physical evolution, including its hidden quantum bath. Introduce two commuting symmetries:

\\[ R=-Z_pZ_q,\qquad S=\operatorname{SWAP}\_{pq}Z_a. \\]

Two coherent check ancillas implement the accepted operation

\\[ \boxed{ U\_{\rm accepted} =\frac14(U+RUR+SUS+RSURS). } \\]

Direct algebra gives

\\[ [U\_{\rm accepted},R]=[U\_{\rm accepted},S]=0. \\]

Consequently, the accepted detector cannot produce a false arrival click from an off-code input. Within the protected dual-rail subspace, its successful branch again has precisely the logical \\(Y/Z\\) structure required by the preceding teleportation-based fault theorem.

### Executed full-memory verification

I implemented the actual coherent-control circuit and compared it with the operator formula, including noncommuting bath dynamics, code leakage and ancilla disturbances.

# 2.6 × 10²

# 1.07 × 10⁻¹⁶

# 0

# 100%

False-click probability for ordinary classical randomization in that example

The distinction between coherent and classical checks is essential. Randomly choosing which symmetry to apply does not enforce the symmetry. The check ancillas must retain coherence across the physical interaction, and their interference outcome must be postselected.

This mechanism is closely related to established Pauli-check sandwiching.
